## Release — backlog-campaign v0.30.0

### ✨ What's new in v0.30.0

#### Catch up to your weekly pace: `/blackhole catchup`

- A new `catchup` mode spends whatever weekly plan quota your day left unused, on real backlog issues, up to a pace floor of 17.5% per weekday, so the quota is not wasted at the weekly reset. The reset day counts as half a day. When you are already at or above the floor, it does nothing ([#1273](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1273)).
- It never pushes the 5-hour window past 80%: new workers stop at 75% and running workers stop at 80%, so interactive work always has room. A new `catchup` config block holds the pace, the caps, the lane and the claim lease ([#1273](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1273)).
- It fails closed: when usage cannot be read, it skips instead of running blind. Normal `run` behaviour is unchanged ([#1273](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1273)).
- Built for a schedule. The playbook ships a scheduled-task prompt, for weekdays around 18:00, 23:00 and 04:00 and every 5 hours on weekends, that hands the host's usage reading to the gate with `--usage-file`. Copy it per account and set that account's `catchup.lane` ([#1273](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1273)).

#### The launch gate covers `run` and `catchup` alike

- Both modes print the whole configuration as an executive summary and ask Accept or Adjust per section before the first worker starts. For `catchup`, the pacing preset (floor, 5-hour caps, lane) is filled in as the defaults, every row stays adjustable for that run, and a Pacing row shows the usage reading and the shortfall. A scheduled run prints the summary and proceeds ([#1273](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1273)).
- `/blackhole stop` drains a catchup exactly like a run ([#1273](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1273)).
- A run started on an installed plugin older than another installed version now says so in one line, instead of silently running older gate logic ([#1271](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/issues/1271)).

#### Usage reading on any host

- `bun run usage` prints one normalized reading wherever the campaign runs (CLI, desktop app, cloud): the plan, only the windows that plan has (5-hour, weekly, per-model weekly) with used % and reset time, extra usage, and where the reading came from ([#1273](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1273)).
- The rate-limit cache reader moved into its own module, which ends an import cycle between the usage source and the pace gate ([#1272](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/issues/1272)).

#### Claims that hold across accounts and colleagues

- Before working an issue, a campaign claims it with an `in-progress:<lane>` label and the account's assignee, and releases the claim on merge, stop or failure. The GitHub, Gitea and GitLab adapters all implement claim and release ([#1273](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1273)).
- Ownership comes from the lane label, not the branch prefix. Two accounts' campaigns therefore no longer treat each other's `blackhole/` branches as their own. A new `lane` config key replaces the hardcoded list, which remains as the fallback ([#1273](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1273)).
- A claim lease (`claim_lease_hours`, default 24) frees an issue whose claim and closing PR have both gone quiet, so a crashed run never holds an issue forever ([#1273](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1273)).

Design record: [ADR-054](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/blob/main/documentation/decisions/ADR-054-catchup-mode-quota-pacing.md).
